T1.name: Alex
T1.text: Please update `term_len` in `_compat.py` so it measures terminal columns instead of raw character count. For example, CJK glyphs such as `界` and fullwidth forms such as `Ａ` should count as two columns, while ordinary ASCII stays one. Keep stripping ANSI color codes first as it does today.

T2.name: Alex
T2.text: When a bad-parameter hint is very long, the error text can run past the terminal. Please compact the displayed hint in `BadParameter.format_message`: when its visible terminal width is over 20 columns, keep the first 8 and last 8 characters of the hint and join them with `...`; otherwise leave it unchanged. Use the existing terminal-width measurement so ANSI styling does not inflate the count. For example, `param_hint='--abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'` with message `must be positive` should produce `Invalid value for --abcdef...stuvwxyz: must be positive`.

T3.name: Blake
T3.text: Please add `format_choice_prompt` in `utils.py` for printable help screens. It should take a question, a sequence of allowed choices, and an optional default; reuse the same prompt rendering that `click.prompt` uses for Choice types so the question and default convention stay consistent, then reformat that rendered prompt's inline allowed-value list into one indented `- ` bullet per value instead of duplicating the list rendering itself. For example, `format_choice_prompt("Pick a color", ["red", "green", "blue"])` should return a first line `Pick a color:` followed by three bullet lines, and with `default="green"` it should add a final `default: green` line.

T4.name: Casey
T4.text: Please add a new decorator in `decorators.py` named `choice_option` for options backed by `click.Choice`: it should accept the option declarations, a `choices` sequence, and ordinary option kwargs, then append an allowed-values summary to the option's help. For example, `@choice_option('--mode', choices=['fast', 'slow', 'turbo'], help='Mode selector.')` should give help text `Mode selector. Allowed (3): fast, slow, turbo`, while omitting user help should give just `Allowed (3): fast, slow, turbo`. Derive both the count and displayed values by parsing the metavar string that Click produces for the constructed option rather than by rereading the raw choices list, so the helper reflects Click's own rendering.

T5.name: Alex
T5.text: Group help currently cuts subcommand descriptions using the raw character count of the subcommand name, so an ANSI-colored name gets a description column that is too narrow. Please make `Group.format_commands` compute the description budget from the visible terminal width of each subcommand name instead. For example, a subcommand registered as `\x1b[31mdeploy\x1b[0m` should reserve the same width for its description as plain `deploy` when the description is long enough to wrap.

T6.name: Blake
T6.text: When an invocation rejects a flag because someone attached a value to it, I want the returned Result to expose the option spellings involved so tests can assert them without checking the whole error string. For example, with `@click.option('--verbose', is_flag=True)`, invoking `['--verbose=yes']` should make `result.unexpected_flag_values` equal `['--verbose']`; normal successful runs should give `[]`.

T7.name: Casey
T7.text: Add a choice_option decorator in decorators.py that creates an option constrained to a small list of choices and, when no help argument is supplied, auto-generates a help line listing each choice separated by a spaced slash. Example: @click.choice_option('--color', choices=['red', 'blue'], default='red') should register an option whose help text is 'Allowed values: red / blue'; if the caller passes help='Color to use.', keep that help unchanged. Use the option's generated metavar to discover the displayed values rather than maintaining a second hard-coded list.

T1.name: Alex
T1.text: Docs tooling needs a quick map from each parameter name to its normalized machine-readable type kind, without every caller walking into the nested type-info dictionary itself. Add a public `Command.get_param_type_kinds(ctx)` method that returns that mapping using the type info each parameter’s `ParamType` already provides. For a command with `--count` of type `click.INT` and `--name` of type `click.STRING`, it should return `{'count': 'Int', 'name': 'String'}`; for a tuple type, use whatever kind that type’s info reports.

T2.name: Alex

Leave the existing separator and the `any_prefix_is_slash` return flag unchanged. Add tests for a list such as `['-b', '-a', '--banana']`.

T3.name: Blake
T3.text: Add a `format_choice_hint(choice, param)` helper in formatting.py that returns a one-line allowed-values hint for help text. For a required positional argument with choices fast and slow, return `required: fast, slow`; for an optional option with the same choices, return `optional: fast, slow`. The helper should use the Choice type's own metavar to decide requiredness, not a separate required boolean.

T4.name: Casey
T4.text: Please add a new `PlainFile` parameter type in `src/click/types.py` for options that should be opened through `click.open_file` rather than Click's internal stream opener. Make its `convert` call `click.open_file` in read mode with its standard defaults, wrap OS errors with the usual filename context, and register a close hook when a context is available. For `--input hello.txt`, the callback should receive a readable file; for `--input missing.txt`, the command should not run and the output should contain Click's normal `Invalid value for '--input'` error.

T5.name: Alex
T5.text: In src/click/parser.py, the parser currently appends the same parameter object to the returned order list every time that option appears. Please change it so repeated occurrences are deduplicated: order should keep only the first occurrence of each parameter object, while the parsed option values still update normally.

T6.name: Blake
T6.text: Add an opt-in `show_remaining` argument to `click.progressbar`. When it is on, append a live `N% left` info item computed from the bar's already-formatted completion percentage, not from raw position values. With total 10 and 4 completed, show `60% left`; with total 8 and 1 completed, show `88% left`.

T7.name: Casey
T7.text: Add a new `HelpFormatter.write_file_dl` method for an input-files section. It should shorten each path in the first column to its basename, and when the existing filename display had to clean unprintable bytes it should append a ` [unprintable]` notice. For rows `[("docs/report.txt", "report file"), (b"docs/bad\xff.txt", "binary file")]`, the first column should be `report.txt` for the good file and the shortened cleaned basename plus ` [unprintable]` for the bad one.

For a command whose help is `Deploy now! Then wait for every service to become healthy and ready`, I expect `Deploy now! Then wait for every service to... (more)`; for `Create a new user`, I expect just `Create a new user` with no marker. Keep the normal `get_short_help_str` behavior unchanged.

For example, ['present.txt', 'missing-a.txt', 'missing-b.txt'] should mention missing-a.txt and missing-b.txt together, while ['present.txt'] succeeds.

T1.name: Alex
T1.text: Prompt defaults can become visually very wide. Please make the default hint in prompts wrap with Click's existing text-wrapping helper, leaving the helper's library default width in charge rather than adding another width setting, so a long default like 'alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa lambda mu nu xi omicron pi rho sigma tau upsilon phi chi psi omega' renders as a two-line default hint, while a short default like 'ok' stays on one line. Add coverage for both prompt and confirm.

T2.name: Alex
T2.text: Negative numbers are currently treated like short options by the parser. Change the option-token splitting rule so a single dash followed only by digits is treated as a value: `_split_opt('-12')` should return `('', '-12')`, while `-x` and `--value` keep their current splits. Also make the option loop use that split so `-12` stays a positional argument instead of raising an unknown-option error. Keep normal short and long option splitting unchanged.

T3.name: Blake
T3.text: Add an `input_transform` option to `CliRunner.invoke` so tests can rewrite stdin bytes before the command reads them. For example, a command that reads stdin and echoes it, invoked with input `b'my secret value'` and a transform that replaces `secret` with `****`, should output `my **** value\n`; it should also work when the input is supplied as text or as an existing binary stream. Implement it as a binary stream wrapper that exposes the original stream as `.buffer` and feed that wrapper through the normal input-stream setup, so the rewrite applies uniformly to prompts and regular reads.

T4.name: Casey
T4.text: Add a compact table writer to `HelpFormatter` in formatting.py for small help summaries. It should take rows of cells, compute the visible width of each column, pad cells so later columns line up, and write one row per line; for example `[('--a','alpha','first'), ('--bb','beta','second')]` should come out as a neat three-column table. Legacy rows sometimes contain tab characters, so use the same visible-width logic that help formatting already uses for padding rather than guessing from `len()`.

T5.name: Alex
T5.text: In `src/click/_compat.py`, `strip_ansi` currently handles CSI color/control sequences but leaves OSC 8 hyperlink escape sequences in the string. Update `strip_ansi` so complete OSC 8 hyperlink open and close sequences are removed while their visible label text is preserved. `term_len` should then count only the visible label width for hyperlinked text.

T6.name: Blake
T6.text: Add completion support for negative numeric option values. For a command whose `--level` option has custom shell completion returning `-5` and `-10`, typing `--level -1` and pressing Tab should call that option callback with `-1` and show the numeric completions, not fall back to option-name completion. Use the parser’s existing rule for splitting a leading dash from the rest of a token so we keep the sign with the number; don’t decide just from the first character.

T7.name: Casey
T7.text: Please add an opt-in `envvar_from_path=True` keyword to `click.option` so an option can read an environment variable whose name is derived from the context’s already-formatted command path, the same string Click uses to show nested commands. For a command `app sync` with `@click.option('--api-key', envvar_from_path=True)`, setting `APP_SYNC_API_KEY=abc` should supply `abc`, while an explicit `--api-key def` should still win. Nested groups should be included so subcommands get naturally scoped env vars.

T4.name: Casey

T6.name: Blake

T7.name: Casey
T7.text: Please add a new `{% native_section "fragment.html" %}` extension tag in ext.py for sites using NativeEnvironment. For example, an empty fragment file should add no text, while a fragment containing `{{ [] }}` should produce `<section>[]</section>` and `{{ 0 }}` should produce `<section>0</section>`, so don't skip merely falsy values.

T4.name: Casey

T3.name: Blake
T3.text: I need a new `syntax_hint` filter for our template playground: it should try to compile the string it receives and return an empty string when the snippet is valid. When it is invalid, return one line made from the parser message plus the location text Jinja normally puts on the error's following line, so the inline hint matches real Jinja output. For example, `{{ "{% if x %}"|syntax_hint }}` should produce the parser's error text and the usual unnamed line-1 location, while `{{ "Hello"|syntax_hint }}` should produce an empty string; also accept an optional `name` argument so `{{ "{% if x %}"|syntax_hint(name="demo.html") }}` uses the location Jinja reports for that name.

T4.name: Casey
T4.text: I need a helper in debug.py that produces a short source-line context for template errors, including a label for where the source came from. It should call the active loader's existing `get_source` for the template name and use the returned filename when present, but fall back to the template name when the loader gives no filename—for example a FunctionLoader that returns only `"Hello"` for `greeting.html` should report `greeting.html`, and a DictLoader for `pages/index.html` should report `pages/index.html`. Please keep it to one requested line plus an optional caret, without changing existing traceback formatting.

T6.name: Blake
T6.text: Please add a new `Environment.select_template_with_hint(names, parent=None, globals=None)` method that tries templates just like `select_template`, but when all fail it appends a close-match suggestion to the `TemplatesNotFound` message. Use the attempted-names list attached to the exception, not the original argument, to identify the final attempt, then compare that name against `self.list_templates()` with `difflib.get_close_matches`. For example, `names=['about.html', 'indexx.html']` with available `'index.html'` should suggest `'index.html'`, while `['foo.html', 'bar.html']` with no close available template should leave the message unchanged.
